quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when you slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: When you approach a dangerous area like an intersection, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good reason for choosing your lane position?

options.text: Help other drivers see you and you see them.
Stay out of other drivers' blind spots.

questions.explanation: Good lane position should help you see and be seen, avoid blind spots and road hazards, keep others from sharing your lane, and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Which is a poor reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is too close to the car ahead.
Someone is sitting in a parked car.
You want people to notice your motorcycle.
You are passing a pedestrian in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to alert vehicles and pedestrians before you pass them. Use it if a driver in another lane is following too closely, if someone is in a parked car, or if a pedestrian is in the street. Don't use it just to get attention.

questions.question: What is the best formation for a group of riders going through a curve?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation works well for groups traveling straight. Use single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders at the back watch them.

questions.question: Which is NOT a feature of an effective face shield?
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be scratch-free, allow clear side views, fasten securely, and allow air to flow. An airtight shield causes fogging and makes it hard to see.

questions.question: What should you do if rain starts while you are riding?

options.text: Ride down the center of your lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull to the shoulder and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil buildup that is slippery when wet. Ride in tire tracks where other cars have passed. Slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After riding for a long time

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips under five miles long at speeds under 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: What do you NOT need to adjust when carrying a passenger?
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight that changes how your motorcycle sits. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, headlight, and mirrors. You don't need to adjust the brake light.

questions.question: What protects your eyes from the wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, sunglasses, and eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: When applying the front brake, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
Use only two fingers to grab the brake.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.
Stomp hard on the brake lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
questions.explanation: To brake safely, squeeze the brake lever with all four fingers. Apply pressure steadily and smoothly, increasing force as needed.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may encourage the other driver to return to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should not:
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes with smooth, gradual pressure. Never brake suddenly.

questions.question: The effects of marijuana can last for:
questions.explanation: When smoked, marijuana takes effect within minutes and lasts 2-4 hours. When eaten, it takes over an hour to work but can last more than six hours.

questions.question: When riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway, the best group formation is:
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation when traveling on straight roads. Switch to single-file when going through curves, making turns, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their true distance and speed.

questions.question: The center of a lane usually has an oily strip. This area is:

options.text: Usually safe unless the road is wet.
Usually safe unless it is sunny.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from vehicles collects in a strip in the center of lanes. When dry, this area is usually safe for riding. When wet, avoid it. The strip is usually narrow enough that you can ride to one side and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: When you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both at the same time and brake harder.
Do both at the same time, focusing mainly on swerving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: You need good traction to swerve safely, so don't brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: When loading cargo on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Pack lighter items near the front.
Try not to place items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting weight behind the rear axle makes the motorcycle harder to control.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: At night, use your high beam (unless following another vehicle), use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective gear to stay visible. Stay flexible with your lane position to see, be seen, and maintain a safe space cushion.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is usually a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Riders wearing helmets are ________ more likely to survive a crash than those without helmets.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in any crash.

questions.question: If your motorcycle has convex mirrors, you should practice using them because:

options.text: Most people aren't used to using mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they really are.
They make objects look closer than they really are.
It can be difficult to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give you a wider view behind you but make objects seem farther away than they are. Get used to your mirrors before riding.

questions.question: Studies show most riders in crashes:

options.text: Do not use the front brake enough and use the rear brake too much.
Use the front brake too much and do not use the rear brake enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake enough and use the rear brake too much.
questions.explanation: Most riders involved in crashes do not use the front brake enough and use the rear brake too much.

questions.question: Wobbling or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars may be caused by:

options.text: Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.explanation: Wobbles are usually caused by improper loading, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: When parking a motorcycle next to a curb, it should be:

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the parking space so drivers can see it better.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, you should:

options.text: Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride on the left side of the lane.
Always ride on the right side of the lane.
Change your position based on conditions and other factors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position based on conditions and other factors.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Choose where you are most visible and can keep space around you.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane is slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left track is usually best.

questions.question: A rider without a helmet is ________ more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.

questions.question: When a vehicle tries to pass you from behind, you should:

options.text: Move to the center of the lane.
Move to the left side of the lane.
Move to the right side of the lane.
Not worry about your lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Staying too close to the passing vehicle increases crash risk.

questions.question: What should you do to be seen better at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: The best way to help others see you at an intersection is to ride with your headlight on. Keep your headlight on whenever your motorcycle is running.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: It takes up less space on the highway.
The group is easy to see.
The group is unlikely to be split up.
Riders will reach their destination faster in a close group than in a spread out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders will reach their destination faster in a close group than in a spread out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a close group is recommended because it uses less road space, is easier for others to see, and is less likely to get separated at traffic lights or during passes. Speed is not affected by how close together riders are.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When someone is following too closely.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When someone is following too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing if someone is following you too closely. The driver behind you may not see the hazard that is making you slow down. Also flash your brake light if you are slowing down somewhere drivers might not expect it.

questions.question: How should you brake on a slippery surface?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use sudden pressure on the front brake to prevent the front tire from locking.
Use only one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the brake lever slowly to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: When do you NOT need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When there is a lot of traffic.
When you can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more time to stop. You need more distance on slippery pavement, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy and another driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another rider on the left, where should you position yourself in your lane?

options.text: On the right side of the lane so they see you in their side mirror.
On the left side of the lane to see better ahead.
In the center of the lane so they see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave back and forth to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: When preparing to pass on the left, ride on the left side of your lane. This improves your view of the road ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals can be used instead of or with turn signals to communicate with other riders. When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing down, it means the rider is slowing down or stopping.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, why should you ride on the left side of your lane?

options.text: The right side could be slippery.
You can better spot hazards in the next lane.
Drivers don't usually expect to be passed on their left.
It places you in the rearview mirror of the car in front.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can better spot hazards in the next lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when preparing to pass. This position gives you a better view of the road ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What formation should a group of three-wheel motorcycles use?
questions.explanation: Two-wheel motorcycles can use a staggered formation, but three-wheel motorcycles are too wide. A group of three-wheel motorcycles should ride in a single-file line.

questions.question: How can you keep other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Swerve back and forth across your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: To discourage other drivers from trying to share your lane, ride in the center of your lane.

questions.question: Your riding clothes should protect you from all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Your riding clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, and cold. They should also protect you from the motorcycle itself. Good clothing also helps protect you if you crash.

questions.question: The center of the lane often has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
Should always be avoided because other parts of the lane do not have it.
Adds grip for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars drips onto the center of the lane. When the road is dry, this area still has enough grip for safe riding. Since the oily strip is usually only about two feet wide, you can often ride to one side of it and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. The best path through a curve may not follow the curve itself. You may need to move from the outside to the inside of the curve before straightening out.

questions.question: Good footwear for riding a motorcycle:
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on things. Tuck in laces so they do not get caught on anything.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids while braking, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake immediately and re-apply it smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately and re-apply it smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks up while braking, release the front brake right away. Then apply the brake smoothly again.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay in the same lane position and never move.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Only ride in the center of the lane so other drivers see you.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change where you ride in the lane based on road conditions, traffic, and other factors.

questions.question: Do not change gears on railroad tracks because:

options.text: Other drivers may not expect you to change gears.
The uneven surface may make shifting harder.

questions.explanation: Do not shift gears while crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle could stall while you are on the tracks.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best formation is usually:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for group riding. Switch to a single-file line when turning, going through curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way they do not have to chase the group, and experienced riders can watch them from behind.
